items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-07-29
items.q: You had Joe Oliver Day, you had Manuel Perez, you had Kimmer, you had Icon White.

ctx.x: I'm talking about, say, in 1910 when you were just really coming out, who would be in the street playing really tunk music?
Well, we had a good men up in there. You had Joe Oliver Day, you had Manuel Perez, you had Kimmer, you had Icon White. Oh, I couldn't get you the names of all of them.
Yeah, but I mean, non-reading bands, ones that didn't read at all, wouldn't they have those?

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-12-20
items.q: I did hear the band. Buddy Bowling, Marion Perez

ctx.x: I did hear the band. Buddy Bowling, Marion Perez, and Nick Clark Crowe, and all that. And a bunch of them was different bands with the Imperial, the Superior, and Buddy Bowling, and what you called Jim Brown, all them. I remember that. But that was above my time. I wasn't playing. I was trying to play. You see, I was trying to play because I had but one song I played. Hey, what song was that really? That was the Got Good Bullies, so they say. What was that again?
Your Got Good Bullies, so they say.
